slice.hypothesis: Current Chat-exposed Gmail draft and message-label contracts expose a caller-visible stable version/precondition, conditional write, or idempotency key sufficient for a deterministic finite-state coordination cell without richer-mode execution.
slice.tested_surface: Schema-only inspection of create_draft, update_draft, list_drafts, send_draft, create_label, list_labels, apply_labels_to_emails, batch_modify_email, read_email/search contracts as exposed by one Gmail connector discovery batch.
slice.tested_scope: Current Chat-exposed tool schemas only. No Gmail profile, drafts, messages, threads, labels, attachments, recipients, or other user semantic data were read or mutated. No Gmail operation was executed.

evidence.draft_create_contract: create_draft accepts recipient/content/threading inputs but no idempotency key, expected prior state, version, ETag, or caller-supplied request token. A lost response followed by blind retry therefore has no schema-level duplicate-suppression contract.
evidence.draft_update_contract: update_draft accepts draft_id plus replacement fields and preserves omitted fields, but accepts no draft revision, ETag, expected body/subject, compare predicate, or idempotency key. It is a blind overwrite of the identified draft rather than compare-and-set.
evidence.draft_readback_contract: list_drafts exposes summarized draft metadata for selection, while the exposed mutation inputs do not accept any version/read token returned by readback. send_draft accepts only draft_id. No read->expected-version->write atomic binding is expressible.
evidence.message_label_contract: apply_labels_to_emails and batch_modify_email accept message_ids plus label names/IDs to add/remove. They expose no expected current label set, message version, ETag, compare predicate, or idempotency key, so a prior read cannot be atomically bound to a later label transition.
evidence.label_create_contract: create_label explicitly returns the existing label instead of creating a duplicate when the same name already exists. This is a narrow name-deduplicated create behavior, not a mutable finite-state CAS: the caller supplies no expected state/version, the response contract does not provide winner/transition semantics, and no conditional rename/delete/state-transition primitive is exposed in the current Gmail tool set.
evidence.atomicity_consequence: Current schemas provide stable object identifiers and some operation-level deduplication/set-like behavior, but not caller-controlled compare(observed state/version)==expected then mutate(new) as one atomic action.

transversal_comparison.github_sha_cas_from_own_state: Remains the stronger provider-specific generic conditional-write primitive already verified in own state because the write contract accepts the current blob SHA as a caller-supplied precondition. Its live stale-SHA/lost-response retry behavior remains a separate unexecuted future leaf.

slice.measurable_effect: CAS-expressibility checklist: stable object identity=present; caller-supplied expected version/state=absent; atomic compare predicate=absent; write mutation=present; generic idempotency key=absent; narrow duplicate-name suppression=create_label only. Result: generic deterministic finite-state CAS acceptance is false for the tested Gmail schemas.
slice.complexity_resource_estimate: One connector-schema discovery batch; zero user semantic reads/writes; zero hosted compute; zero Gmail operations; no paid/trial/monthly quota consumed by this audit leaf.
failure_edge_cases: A future Gmail connector schema could expose ETags, message/draft history IDs as accepted write preconditions, conditional mutation, or explicit idempotency keys; this result is scoped to the current exposed contracts.
Provider internals may make some repeated label operations idempotent, but the exposed schema still lacks caller-controlled version binding for state transitions.
Gmail label-name deduplication could support a monotone existence marker, but without conditional transition/delete semantics it is not a general mutable coordination cell.

Actual Gmail operation quotas, account prerequisites, mailbox visibility, and incremental monetary cost are not established by schema-only inspection; therefore no Phase-1 zero-quota/cost acceptance is claimed.
